name: fenics-showcase
title: FEniCS showcase: seven real dolfinx studies as composable pbg processes
description:
Seven studies build a rigor-to-showcase arc. `poisson-validation`
verifies the bridge is not just correct but genuinely HIGH-ORDER
accurate: P1/P2/P3 Lagrange elements each hit their own theoretical L2
convergence rate on a smooth manufactured solution. `mesh-convergence`
takes that verified bridge to a corner singularity (the L-shaped domain's
re-entrant corner) and shows a real residual-based a posteriori estimator,
driving Doerfler-marked adaptive refinement, recovers close to the
optimal convergence rate that uniform refinement is provably capped below
-- with the refined mesh visibly concentrating at the singularity.
`transient-diffusion` moves from one-shot solves to TIME-STEPPED,
multi-process composition: an extended `DiffusionProcess` (a Dirichlet
source boundary) and a new `LinearDegradationProcess`, coupled only
through shared stores, reproduce a classic Source-Diffusion-Degradation
morphogen gradient and its Wolpert "French flag" positional-information
readout. `reaction-diffusion` is the investigation's composability
headline: TWO `DiffusionProcess` instances (differential diffusivities)
plus ONE `GrayScottReactionProcess`, wired to shared stores with none of
the three processes aware of the others, produce a genuine 2D Turing
instability -- spontaneous self-organization from a near-uniform field
into structurally distinct spot/labyrinth/stripe-family patterns across
three parameter regimes. Three ADVANCED studies then push the same
bridge into full continuum mechanics: `navier-stokes` is the
fluid-dynamics showpiece -- a von Karman vortex street off an off-center
cylinder (the DFG 2D-2 benchmark: gmsh-generated cylinder-refined mesh,
IPCS operator splitting, coupled P2/P1 velocity-pressure, real
surface-force-integral drag/lift) landing in the neighborhood of the
published reference Cd/Strouhal; `complex-geometry` is the porous-media
showpiece -- a real Taylor-Hood mixed Stokes solve on a gmsh-generated
periodic pillar lattice, with the effective (Darcy) permeability computed
from the solved field and shown to fall monotonically as porosity falls;
`moving-boundary` is the fluid-structure-coupling showpiece --
peristaltic pumping from a genuinely composed system (a harmonic-extension
ALE mesh-motion process prescribing a traveling wall occlusion, coupled
through shared stores to an ALE-corrected incompressible Navier-Stokes
process), producing a net axial flow that is positive and grows with
occlusion amplitude with no term in either process hard-coding the
other's physics. Runs are authored here and executed with results
recorded into the workspace's `.pbg/runs.jsonl` run log; behavior-test
evaluation reads that run log against each study's `expected_behavior`.
question:
Can real FEniCSx (dolfinx) solvers, wrapped as ordinary process-bigraph
Steps/Processes, both PASS rigorous numerical-verification checks and
drive seven genuinely different, showcase-tier physics problems --
spanning high-order accuracy, singular geometry, morphogen patterning,
Turing instability, bluff-body vortex shedding, porous-media flow, and
moving-boundary fluid-structure coupling -- using the same underlying
bridge throughout?
hypothesis:
A single dolfinx bridge, exercised through a handful of composable
process-bigraph building blocks (a Step for stateless one-shot solves, a
Process for time-stepped ones, shared bigraph stores for wiring
independently-authored processes together), is sufficient to reproduce
textbook FEM verification results (optimal P1/P2/P3 convergence rates, a
posteriori-driven adaptive refinement recovering a singularity's optimal
rate) AND to drive substantially harder showcase physics (a two-species
Turing instability, a von Karman vortex street, a porous-media
permeability sweep, an ALE peristaltic pump) without departing from that
same validated bridge or requiring problem-specific solver hacks.

executive.what_is_this:
A showcase investigation proving that a real external FEM solver
(FEniCSx/dolfinx, not a mock or reimplementation), wrapped as ordinary
process-bigraph Steps/Processes, both passes rigorous numerical-
verification checks and drives seven substantially different
showcase-tier physics problems using the same bridge throughout. Two
validation studies (`poisson-validation`, `mesh-convergence`) confirm
numerical fidelity -- optimal multi-order L2 convergence and adaptive
recovery of an optimal rate on a corner singularity. Two dynamics
studies (`transient-diffusion`, `reaction-diffusion`) extend the bridge
to time-stepping and cross-process store-wiring composability, the
latter producing a genuine Turing instability from three
independently-authored processes. Three ADVANCED studies
(`navier-stokes`, `complex-geometry`, `moving-boundary`) push the same
bridge into incompressible Navier-Stokes vortex shedding, a real
porous-media permeability result, and ALE fluid-structure-coupled
peristaltic pumping.
executive.verdict:
Authored and lint-clean: 7 studies, each with a real
`@composite_generator` baseline, a `sims/run.py` canonical runner, and
an interactive viz, with a completed run recorded in
`.pbg/runs.jsonl` for every study. Standalone execution of every runner
reproduces the expected numerics: P1/P2/P3 convergence rates of
1.998/3.000/4.000 against theoretical 2.0/3.0/4.0 (poisson-validation);
adaptive refinement recovering a -0.528 energy-norm convergence rate
(near the theoretical optimal -0.5) against uniform's provably-capped
-0.338, with the adaptive mesh's near-corner cell density growing
55.8x (mesh-convergence); a morphogen gradient whose fitted decay
length matches the analytic lambda=sqrt(D/k) to within 1.63% across
three regimes, with French-flag thresholds shifting monotonically
inward as predicted (transient-diffusion); a genuine, now-mature
Gray-Scott Turing instability -- V's spatial variance grows 10.2-15.5x
across the three regimes from a near-uniform start into a bounded,
structurally non-trivial pattern (the labyrinth regime maturing to 40
disconnected pattern regions), with three (F,k) regimes producing
measurably different coverage/topology (reaction-diffusion); a von
Karman vortex street with a now-saturated oscillating lift coefficient
(std(Cl)=0.736, Cl_max=1.066), mean drag Cd=3.168 (DFG 2D-2 reference
Cd_max~=3.22-3.24, within ~1-2%), and Strouhal St=0.30+/-0.02 (matching
reference ~0.295-0.305) (navier-stokes); a Taylor-Hood Stokes solve
through a porous pillar
lattice that stays approximately divergence-free and exactly no-slip
at every porosity, with effective permeability falling >10x across a
4-point porosity sweep (complex-geometry); and an ALE-coupled
peristaltic pump whose net flow rate is clearly positive and increases
monotonically across an amplitude sweep, with the domain measurably
(and exactly, per the traveling-wave geometry) narrowed by wall motion
(moving-boundary).
executive.verdict_detail:
All 7 studies were rebuilt into their current (impressive-tier) form
and are individually lint-clean and executable, with a completed
production run for each recorded in `.pbg/runs.jsonl` (done). This
integration pass bound the investigation narrative and
`acceptance_criteria` to the rebuilt studies' actual
`expected_behavior` names, removed the now-orphaned obstacle/L-shape/
annulus gmsh-Poisson code the porous-lattice study superseded, and
republished the read-only dashboard bundle (done). Not yet done:
driving these runners' completed runs through the dashboard's Tests
tab evaluator against the behavior tests declared below (the
PASS/FAIL verdicts above come from each runner script's own printed
checks, not yet the dashboard's evaluator), and mesh-/dt-convergence
studies for navier-stokes and complex-geometry (both are currently a
single production mesh/dt point chosen for feasible wall-time, not a
convergence study in their own right).

scientific_argument.main_claim:
A real dolfinx bridge, wrapped as ordinary process-bigraph Steps and
Processes, is simultaneously RIGOROUS (reproducing textbook multi-order
FEM convergence theory and a posteriori-driven adaptive refinement) and
COMPOSABLE (independently-authored processes, wired only through shared
bigraph stores, produce emergent physics -- a morphogen gradient, a
Turing instability, a peristaltic pump -- that no single process
computes alone) and capable of ADVANCED continuum-mechanics showcase
results (a DFG-benchmark vortex street, a porous-media permeability
sweep) without departing from the bridge validated by the first two
studies.
evidence_for: poisson-validation: P1/P2/P3 Lagrange elements achieve L2 convergence rates of 1.998/3.000/4.000 against their theoretical optima 2.0/3.0/4.0 on a smooth (sin(pi x)sin(pi y)) manufactured solution -- the bridge is high-order-accurate, not merely correct at one order.

mesh-convergence: on the L-shaped re-entrant-corner singularity, uniform refinement's energy-norm rate is provably capped near -1/3 (achieved -0.338, matching theory almost exactly); a real residual error estimator driving Doerfler-marked adaptive refinement recovers -0.528 (near the theoretical optimal -0.5) and grows the mesh's near-corner cell density 55.8x relative to the initial mesh -- direct geometric evidence the estimator concentrates refinement where the singularity actually is.

transient-diffusion: an extended DiffusionProcess (Dirichlet source boundary) and a new LinearDegradationProcess, coupled purely through shared stores, reproduce the classic SDD morphogen gradient -- fitted decay length within 1.63% of analytic lambda=sqrt(D/k) across 3 regimes, with French-flag threshold crossings shifting monotonically inward as k increases.

reaction-diffusion: two DiffusionProcess instances (species U, V; Du=2*Dv) and one GrayScottReactionProcess, coupled purely through shared stores, produce a genuine, now-mature Turing instability -- V's spatial variance grows 10.2x (baseline) / 10.5x (labyrinth) / 15.5x (stripes) from a near-uniform start, the pattern is bounded and structurally non-trivial (48.0% baseline domain coverage, not all or none of it), and three (F,k) regimes produce measurably different coverage/topology (a 0.196 coverage spread, and 40-vs-1 connected pattern regions between the labyrinth and other regimes -- the labyrinth's blob count roughly quadrupled from the earlier onset-only-sizing run, now unambiguously a labyrinth).

navier-stokes: flow past an off-center cylinder (DFG 2D-2 benchmark, Re=100) sheds a genuine von Karman vortex street that has now reached a saturated limit cycle -- the lift coefficient oscillates (std(Cl)=0.736, Cl_max=1.066, matching/slightly exceeding the DFG reference Cl_max~=0.99-1.01) once past the impulsive-start transient, mean drag Cd=3.168 lands within ~1-2% of the DFG reference Cd_max~=3.22-3.24, and the shedding Strouhal number St=0.30+/-0.02 lands directly on the DFG reference ~0.295-0.305.

complex-geometry: a real Taylor-Hood mixed Stokes solve on a gmsh-generated periodic pillar lattice stays approximately divergence-free (mean|div(u)| ~3e-5-1e-4) and exactly no-slip on every wall/pillar boundary dof at every porosity in a 4-point sweep, and the effective (Darcy) permeability k_eff falls >10x from the sparsest to the densest lattice -- the qualitative Kozeny-Carman-type trend expected of a real porous microstructure.

moving-boundary: a harmonic-extension ALE mesh-motion process and an ALE-corrected incompressible Navier-Stokes process, coupled purely through shared stores, produce genuine peristaltic pumping -- a clearly positive, post-transient net flow rate (Q~=0.19-0.2) that increases monotonically across an amplitude sweep, with the FEM-assembled domain measure exactly (per the traveling-wave geometry) 15% below the undeformed area, confirming the wall motion genuinely deforms the domain rather than sitting inert.
evidence_against: All seven studies use a single fixed random-free deterministic setup (one resolution/degree/parameter point per study beyond the declared sweeps); broader parameter robustness beyond the declared sweeps (resolution in mesh-convergence beyond the AMR levels, rate in reaction-diffusion, amplitude/mode in moving-boundary, lattice density/mesh grading in complex-geometry) is untested. navier-stokes and complex-geometry in particular are each a single production mesh/dt point chosen for feasible wall-time, not mesh- or dt-convergence studies in their own right.

Behavior tests are authored in every study.yaml but not yet driven through the dashboard's Tests tab against the workspace's `.pbg/runs.jsonl` run log, so the PASS/FAIL verdicts above come from the runner scripts' own printed checks, not yet the dashboard's evaluator.
caveats: The coupling-composability claim is demonstrated for three wiring patterns (DiffusionProcess+LinearDegradationProcess for the morphogen gradient, 2x DiffusionProcess+GrayScottReactionProcess for Turing patterns, and the ALE mesh-motion+Navier-Stokes pairing for peristalsis); it has not been exercised against a fourth, unrelated process family to further stress-test that the wiring pattern generalizes beyond diffusion/reaction/flow processes.

The classic Gray-Scott 'spots' regime (F=0.035, k=0.065) was found subcritical for this composite's Du/Dv/dt/domain-size combination during development; the study's three regimes (coral/mitosis-like, labyrinth, stripes) were chosen because they were verified to grow robustly, not because they are the only regimes worth showing. An extended production run (resolution/step-count roughly 2-3x the earlier onset-only sizing) now reaches materially more mature texture -- most visibly the labyrinth regime's blob count growing from ~9 to 40 disconnected regions -- though it is still a finite-time snapshot, not a fully saturated, infinite-time steady-state texture -- see the study report.

The three advanced studies (navier-stokes, complex-geometry, moving-boundary) each stand on their own dolfinx bridge exercise -- the porous lattice is not deforming, the vortex street is not flowing through a porous medium, and moving-boundary's peristalsis is not itself set in a complex (non-rectangular) geometry -- so the showcase demonstrates breadth of individual advanced capability, not a single combined composite exercising all three at once.

moving-boundary's ALE mesh-motion scheme (pure Laplacian smoothing) is honestly reported to degrade (shrinking, and on finer meshes inverting, cell areas) above occlusion amplitude~0.45-0.5 regardless of timestep or mesh refinement; the amplitude sweep used (<=0.4) was chosen to stay safely below that empirically-observed degeneracy onset, not because the mesh-motion scheme is unconditionally robust.

studies.name: poisson-validation
studies.title: High-order accuracy verification: P1/P2/P3 optimal L2 convergence
studies.question:
Do P1, P2, and P3 Lagrange elements each achieve their OWN theoretically
optimal L2 convergence rate (degree+1: 2, 3, 4 respectively) when solving
the dolfinx-backed `PoissonSolverStep` on a smooth (C-infinity)
manufactured solution, or does any element order under- or over-perform
its textbook rate?

studies.name: mesh-convergence
studies.title: Adaptive mesh refinement: recovering optimal convergence on a corner singularity
studies.question:
On the classic L-shaped-domain re-entrant-corner Laplace singularity --
where the exact solution's gradient blows up at the corner and UNIFORM
refinement is provably capped at a suboptimal convergence rate -- does a
real residual-based a posteriori error estimator, driving Doerfler-marked
ADAPTIVE refinement, concentrate elements at the corner and recover
near-optimal convergence?

studies.name: transient-diffusion
studies.title: Morphogen gradient: Source-Diffusion-Degradation (French flag)
studies.question:
Do two independently-authored processes -- ``DiffusionProcess`` (extended
with a real Dirichlet source boundary c=c0 at x=0) and
``LinearDegradationProcess`` (the pure-numpy rate ``-k*c``), coupled ONLY
through shared bigraph stores -- produce a genuine exponential morphogen
gradient c(x) = c0*exp(-x/lambda) at steady state, with decay length
lambda = sqrt(D/k) matching the classic Source-Diffusion-Degradation (SDD)
analytic prediction, when driven through process-bigraph's own Composite
tick loop? And do Wolpert "French flag" positional-information thresholds
applied to that gradient partition the domain into 3 fate regions whose
boundaries shift predictably as lambda shrinks?

studies.name: reaction-diffusion
studies.title: Turing patterns: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion (headline)
studies.question:
Do three independently-authored processes -- TWO ``DiffusionProcess``
instances (one per species, U at Du and V at Dv=Du/2, each with no
knowledge of reactions) and ONE ``GrayScottReactionProcess`` (no knowledge
of FEM/diffusion) -- produce a genuine 2D Turing instability when wired to
the same bigraph stores: does a near-uniform field spontaneously
self-organize into spots/stripes/labyrinth patterns, with none of the
three processes calling into either of the others?

studies.name: navier-stokes
studies.title: Navier-Stokes: von Karman vortex street (DFG 2D-2 benchmark)
studies.question:
Does a real dolfinx incompressible Navier-Stokes solve -- Taylor-Hood-ish
P2/P1 velocity/pressure, classic IPCS operator splitting, on a
gmsh-generated channel-with-cylinder mesh -- reproduce the DFG 2D-2
benchmark's von Karman vortex street: periodic, self-sustaining vortex
shedding off an off-center cylinder, with drag/lift coefficients and a
Strouhal number in the neighborhood of the published reference values?

studies.name: complex-geometry
studies.title: Complex geometry: Stokes flow through a porous pillar lattice
studies.question:
Does a real gmsh-constructed periodic array of circular pillars --
imported into dolfinx via `dolfinx.io.gmsh.model_to_mesh` -- support a
genuine steady Stokes (creeping) flow solve, driven by a prescribed
pressure drop, that stays approximately divergence-free and exactly
no-slip on every pillar and channel wall, and does the effective (Darcy)
permeability computed from that flow DECREASE monotonically as the
lattice's porosity decreases -- the Kozeny-Carman-type physical trend
expected of any real porous microstructure?

studies.name: moving-boundary
studies.title: Peristaltic pumping: traveling-wave wall occlusion ⊕ ALE Navier-Stokes
studies.question:
Does composing a mesh-motion process (a real harmonic-extension ALE
solve, prescribing a traveling-wave occlusion on a channel's walls) with
a flow process (real IPCS incompressible Navier-Stokes, ALE-corrected for
the moving mesh), coupled ONLY through shared bigraph stores, reproduce
genuine peristaltic pumping -- a net axial flow rate that is positive
(in the wave's direction) and grows with the occlusion amplitude -- from
a real dolfinx solve, with no term in either process hard-coding the
other's physics?
